# Learning objectives:

1. Understand the costs and benefits of different mutualistic relationships
2. Incorporate positive interactions in a consumer-resource model

*density dependence, other plant species, and natural enemies limit population growth*

*today focusing on processes that would increase population growth*

# Terminology

* symbiosis: any relationship between species *broad term, can be + or -, includes parasitism*
* mutualism: specific symbiosis, both species benefit
* commensalism: specific symbiosis, 1 benefits, 1 neutral

# Facilitation

* Interspecific, nurse plants in arid environment

*Draw number of interspecific neighbors on x, individual fecundity on y, multiple lines for multiple stress levels (rain shelter, natural, supplemental rain): stress increasing, favorable decreasing; slopes highlight this change*

* Intraspecific, plant-soil feedbacks

*could alter previous plot to intraspecific neighbors on x*

* Benefits: increased vital rates in favorable environment
* Costs: competition for space or other resources

# Pollination

* pollinators get nutrients, plants get fertilization/higher reproduction
* Benefits: quality seeds, genetic variation *outcrossing, compared to self-pollination, wind pollination*
* Costs: dependent on animal density, nectar production, cross-contamination *pollen from other plants not your own*

# Mycorrhizal fungi

* Endomycorrhiza: fungi in root cells, arbuscular mycorrhiza *found in many plant taxa, others specialize*
* Ectomycorrhiza: fungi influence root cells but not inside cell, trees and shrubs
* fungi explore efficiently
  + example: extend beyond normal root zone in crops & get farther nutrients
  + drought resistance in tomatoes and peppers
* fungi get carbohydrates, plants get nutrients 
* Benefits: get nutrients or water in resource-poor environments
* Costs: increased carbon costs *fungi take carbs from plant, so are carbon sink*

# Modeling

* herbivore as pollinator - life stage-dependent 
  + example: butterflies & moths
  + larval/caterpillar: herbivore
  + adults: pollinator

* $p$ - pollination rate
* $h_p$ - handling time per flower
* $H$ - insect herbivore/pollinator abundance
* $M$ - mutualism benefit, proportion

$$M = \frac{p H}{1 + p h_p H}$$

* effect on fecundity
* $f_\mu$ - mean fecundity
* fecundity increased if pollinators present

$$f_{eff} = f_\mu (1 + M)$$

* affects plant pops, not herbs
* in plant paps, affects new seeds, not seedbank or seeds consumed:

$$P_t = \frac{f_\mu g  N_t} {1 + \alpha g N_t}$$
